readings: Using each order's account and that account's branch district, list exactly 10 accounts with the largest difference between their number of orders and the average number of orders per account (averaged over accounts that have at least one order). Break ties by smaller account id first, so that exactly 10 rows are returned. For each one show the account id, the region of its branch (district.A3), its order count and the unrounded difference (order count minus the average), largest difference first.

Using each order's account and that account's branch district, list every account whose rank by the difference between its number of orders and the average number of orders per account (averaged over accounts that have at least one order) is within the top 10, using ranking with ties. All accounts tied at the 10th-ranked difference are included, so more than 10 rows may be returned. For each one show the account id, the region of its branch (district.A3), its order count and the unrounded difference (order count minus the average), largest difference first.
queries:
SELECT o.account_id,
       d.A3,
       COUNT(*) AS order_count,
       COUNT(*) - (SELECT AVG(cnt) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM "order" GROUP BY account_id)) AS diff
FROM "order" o
JOIN account a ON a.account_id = o.account_id
JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id
GROUP BY o.account_id, d.A3
ORDER BY diff DESC, o.account_id ASC
LIMIT 10;
WITH oc AS (
    SELECT o.account_id, d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS order_count
    FROM "order" o
    JOIN account a ON o.account_id = a.account_id
    JOIN district d ON a.district_id = d.district_id
    GROUP BY o.account_id, d.A3
),
diffs AS (
    SELECT account_id, region, order_count,
           order_count - (SELECT AVG(order_count) FROM oc) AS diff
    FROM oc
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT account_id, region, order_count, diff,
           RANK() OVER (ORDER BY diff DESC) AS rnk
    FROM diffs
)
SELECT account_id, region, order_count, diff
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk <= 10
ORDER BY diff DESC;
